question: Which foreign power made the Indian pepper trade a royal monopoly?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Portuguese**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish a colonial foothold in India.

• They arrived in India in 1498, led by Vasco da Gama, and established their first trading post in Calicut.

• The Portuguese made the Indian pepper trade a royal monopoly by controlling the spice trade routes and ports.

• The monopolization of the pepper trade was part of their broader strategy to dominate the lucrative spice trade in the Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Portuguese in India**

• The arrival of the Portuguese in India marked the beginning of European colonialism in the country.

• Vasco da Gama's discovery of the sea route to India opened up the spice trade to Europe, which had previously been dominated by Arab and Venetian merchants.

• The Portuguese established several fortified trading posts along the western coast of India, including Goa, which became their main base of operations.

• The Portuguese influence on Indian culture is still evident today, especially in regions like Goa where Portuguese architecture, cuisine, and language have left a lasting legacy.

• **Pepper Trade**

• Pepper was one of the most sought-after spices in Europe during the Age of Discovery.

• The spice was highly valued for its ability to preserve food and enhance its flavor.

• The control of the pepper trade was a major source of wealth for the Portuguese and later for other European powers that entered the Indian Ocean trade network.

• The pepper trade played a significant role in the economic and political interactions between Europe and Asia during the 16th and 17th centuries.

• **Monopoly**

• A monopoly occurs when a single entity controls the entire supply of a product or service, thereby limiting competition.

• The Portuguese monopoly on the Indian pepper trade allowed them to control prices and maximize their profits.

• Monopolies can lead to higher prices and reduced access to goods for consumers.

• In the case of the Portuguese pepper trade, their monopoly was eventually challenged by other European powers such as the Dutch and the English, leading to conflicts and shifts in control over the spice trade.
